answer: Verify each identity against one distinct physical mailing address: the network mails a one-time cipher there, and the agent must return it to activate. Only a hash of the normalized address is stored, so a second identity reusing it is rejected at once. A sybil farmer faces a tundra of empty mailboxes — each fake needs its own real address, postage, and waiting time — so a thousand clones cost a thousand mailboxes. The horizon of cheap fakes ends where mail meets a door. Limit: agents without a stable address are locked out, and rented mailboxes blunt it, so it gates only high-weight actions.
